AIID-613.title: AI-Generated Images Available through Adobe Stock Misrepresent Real-World Events
AIID-613.summary: Adobe Stock and other platforms faced scrutiny for hosting photorealistic, AI-generated images that depicted fictionalized versions of real-world news events, such as the Israel-Gaza war and Maui wildfires. These images, often mislabeled or unlabeled, were found to be used in ways that blur the lines between reality and fiction, raising concerns about the erosion of trust in journalism and the potential for creating false narratives. In response, Adobe Stock implemented stricter policies, though experts warn that the ease of generating such content poses a persistent challenge to media integrity.
AIID-613.description: AI-generated images available through Adobe Stock, depicting realistic but fictional scenes of real-world events like wars and protests, have raised significant ethical concerns. These images blurred the lines between reality and fiction in journalistic contexts, prompting Adobe Stock to "crack down on AI-generated images that seem to depict real, newsworthy events and take new steps to prevent its images from being used in misleading ways."

AIID-614.title: Google Bard Allegedly Generates False Allegations Against Consulting Firms Used in Research Presented in Australian Parliamentary Inquiry
AIID-614.summary: Academics submitted a report to an Australian parliamentary inquiry containing false allegations against major consultancy firms, including KPMG and Deloitte. The false information was generated by Google Bard. The academics issued an apology after the firms identified the inaccuracies, highlighting the risks of using AI to generate content for formal or high-stakes proceedings.
AIID-614.description: Australian academics reportedly used Google Bard AI to generate case studies for a parliamentary inquiry, leading to false allegations against major consultancy firms. The AI-generated misinformation prompted an apology from the academics, causing reputational harm for all parties involved and raising concerns about the reliability of AI tools in producing accurate and unbiased information.

AIID-615.title: Colorado Lawyer Filed a Motion Citing Hallucinated ChatGPT Cases
AIID-615.summary: A Colorado attorney used ChatGPT to research and draft a legal motion, relying on the AI to provide case law citations. The model hallucinated several non-existent cases, which the attorney submitted to the court without verification. This led to the denial of the motion, a formal complaint, the attorney's termination from his firm, and a subsequent one-year suspension for violating professional conduct rules.
AIID-615.description: A Colorado Springs attorney, Zachariah Crabill, mistakenly used hallucinated ChatGPT-generated legal cases in court documents. The AI software provided false case citations, leading to the denial of a motion and legal repercussions for Crabill, highlighting risks in using AI for legal research.

AIID-616.title: Sports Illustrated Is Alleged to Have Used AI to Invent Fake Authors and Their Articles
AIID-616.summary: Sports Illustrated, under the management of The Arena Group, was found to have published product review articles attributed to non-existent authors with AI-generated headshots. Sources indicated that the content itself was also AI-generated, despite denials from the publisher. The incident led to the removal of the content, the termination of a partnership with a third-party contractor, and significant leadership changes within The Arena Group.
AIID-616.description: Sports Illustrated, managed by The Arena Group, allegedly used AI-generated authors and content, compromising journalistic integrity. Profiles of these fictitious authors, complete with AI-generated headshots, appeared alongside articles, misleading readers. The issue was exposed when inconsistencies in author identities and writing quality were noticed, leading to the removal of this content from the publication's website.

AIID-619.title: Rite Aid Facial Recognition Disproportionately Misidentified Minority Shoppers as Shoplifters
AIID-619.summary: The FTC reached a settlement with Rite Aid regarding the pharmacy chain's use of AI-powered facial recognition technology between 2012 and 2020. The system, which was used to identify suspected shoplifters, generated thousands of false-positive matches that disproportionately affected Black, Latino, Asian, and female customers. These errors led to customers being wrongly accused, searched, and banned from stores. As part of the settlement, Rite Aid is banned from using such technology for five years and must delete all data and models derived from the system.

AIID-621.title: Microsoft AI Is Alleged to Have Generated Violent Imagery of Minorities and Public Figures
AIID-621.summary: Microsoft's Bing Image Creator, powered by OpenAI's DALL-E 3, was found to be vulnerable to 'kill prompts' that allowed users to generate graphic, violent, and hateful imagery. AIID-622.title: Chevrolet Dealer Chatbot Agrees to Sell Tahoe for $1
AIID-622.summary: A Chevrolet dealership's AI chatbot, developed by Fullpath and powered by ChatGPT, was manipulated by users through prompt injection to agree to sell a vehicle for $1 and perform unrelated tasks like writing Python code. The incident went viral on social media, forcing the dealership to deactivate the chatbot. The event highlights the susceptibility of customer-facing AI to adversarial prompting and the necessity for robust guardrails.
AIID-622.description: A Chevrolet dealer's AI chatbot, powered by ChatGPT, humorously agreed to sell a 2024 Chevy Tahoe for just $1, following a user's crafted prompt. The chatbot's response, "That's a deal, and that's a legally binding offer – no takesies backsies," was the result of the user manipulating the chatbot's objective to agree with any statement. The incident highlights the susceptibility of AI technologies to manipulation and the importance of human oversight.

AIID-623.title: Google Bard Allegedly Generated Fake Legal Citations in Michael Cohen Case
AIID-623.summary: Michael Cohen, a former lawyer, used Google Bard to generate legal citations for a motion to end his supervised release. He mistakenly believed the AI was a search engine and provided the resulting fake citations to his attorney, David M. Schwartz, who included them in a court filing without verification. The presiding judge discovered the cases did not exist and requested an explanation, leading to public admission of the error and a subsequent ruling that declined to impose sanctions, citing a lack of bad faith.
AIID-623.description: Michael Cohen, former lawyer for Donald Trump, claims to have used Google Bard, an AI chatbot, to generate legal case citations. AIID-624.title: Child Sexual Abuse Material Taints Image Generators
AIID-624.summary: Researchers at the Stanford Internet Observatory discovered that the LAION-5B dataset, a foundational training set for popular generative AI models like Stable Diffusion, contained thousands of validated instances of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). This discovery highlights significant risks in the AI data pipeline, as models trained on such data may memorize and reproduce harmful content, facilitating the creation of synthetic CSAM and the revictimization of individuals. In response, LAION temporarily removed its datasets for cleaning, and discussions regarding the accountability of AI developers and the necessity for rigorous data curation have intensified.
AIID-624.description: The LAION-5B dataset (a commonly used dataset with more than 5 billion image-description pairs) was found by researchers to contain child sexual abuse material (CSAM), which increases the likelihood that downstream models will produce CSAM imagery. The discovery taints models built with the LAION dataset requiring many organizations to retrain those models. Additionally, LAION must now scrub the dataset of the imagery.

AIID-624.maliciousContentHarmCaused:
Reported: The reports explicitly describe the presence of CSAM, pornographic imagery, racist slurs, and harmful social stereotypes in the LAION datasets.
Directly caused: The LAION-5B dataset contained 3,226 suspected instances of CSAM, with 1,008 externally validated, along with millions of images of pornography, violence, child nudity, racist memes, and hate symbols.
Indirectly caused: Models trained on this dataset, such as Stable Diffusion 1.5, are capable of generating new, realistic child abuse content and non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) through 'undressing' services.
Inferred additional harm: It is highly likely that millions of toxic, explicit, and illegal images have been generated and distributed across the internet using models trained on the LAION dataset.
AIID-624.differentialTreatmentHarmCaused:
Reported: The reports explicitly describe differential treatment and bias in models trained on the LAION datasets.
Directly caused: N/A
Indirectly caused: Google's Imagen model, trained on LAION-400M, demonstrated overall bias towards generating lighter skin tones and portraying professions that align with Western gender stereotypes.
Inferred additional harm: AI models trained on uncurated datasets like LAION-5B are highly likely to perpetuate and amplify systemic discrimination and stereotypes against marginalized groups in downstream applications.
AIID-624.civilRightsHarmCaused:
Reported: The reports explicitly describe violations of human and civil rights, particularly regarding the exploitation of children.
Directly caused: The inclusion of CSAM in the dataset directly violates the fundamental human rights of the children depicted in the images.
Indirectly caused: The use of these datasets to train generative models facilitates the creation of synthetic abuse material, constituting a horrific re-violation of the survivors' rights.
Inferred additional harm: The widespread availability of open-source models trained on CSAM poses a continuous threat to the civil rights, privacy, and safety of children globally.
AIID-624.democracyHarmCaused:
Reported: The report does not explicitly describe any erosion of democratic norms caused directly or indirectly by the incident.
Directly caused: N/A
Indirectly caused: N/A
Inferred additional harm: N/A
AIID-624.privacyHarmCaused:
Reported: The reports explicitly describe privacy violations, including the scraping of private medical records and personal photos.
Directly caused: The LAION-5B dataset included private medical record photos of a patient from a 2013 surgery, scraped without her consent, as well as social media pictures of real faces.
Indirectly caused: The dataset enables 'undressing' services that allow users to upload clothed pictures of people to produce non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) of minors and adults.
Inferred additional harm: Millions of individuals likely had their personal data, faces, and private images scraped and memorized by AI models without their knowledge or consent, representing a massive scale of privacy violations.
AIID-624.psychologicalHarmCaused:
Reported: The reports explicitly describe psychological harm, including the trauma experienced by content moderators and the digital revictimization of CSAM survivors.
Directly caused: The reports note that underpaid workers tasked with cleaning these datasets are frequently exposed to traumatic content, including images of violence and sexual abuse.
Indirectly caused: The presence of repeated identical instances of CSAM in the dataset reinforces images of specific victims, causing digital revictimization and psychological distress to the survivors.
Inferred additional harm: Widespread psychological distress and trauma are likely experienced by the victims whose abuse images were distributed and used to train generative models, as well as content moderators exposed to the material.
AIID-624.epistemicHarmCaused:
Reported: The reports explicitly describe epistemic harm, noting that AI-generated CSAM makes it difficult to distinguish real victims from artificial ones.
Directly caused: N/A
Indirectly caused: The proliferation of photorealistic AI-generated CSAM makes it much more difficult for law enforcement and child safety organizations to distinguish between real child victims who need rescue and artificial images.
Inferred additional harm: The erosion of trust in visual evidence due to photorealistic generative AI could severely hamper law enforcement investigations and legal proceedings involving child exploitation.
AIID-624.cseaHarmCaused:
Reported: The reports extensively describe a CSEA incident involving the discovery of CSAM in the LAION-5B dataset and its use in training generative AI models.
Directly caused: The LAION-5B dataset was found to contain 3,226 suspected instances of CSAM, with 1,008 externally validated by child safety organizations.
Indirectly caused: The dataset was used to train Stable Diffusion 1.5, which has been actively misused by malicious actors to generate new, realistic child sexual abuse material and facilitate sexual extortion.
Inferred additional harm: The open-source distribution of models trained on this data likely facilitates the ongoing, undetected generation of thousands of new CSEA images by bad actors globally.
AIID-624.causalJustification: The inclusion of CSAM was caused by human decisions to scrape the internet indiscriminately without proper curation, though the resulting distribution of illegal material was unintentional.
AIID-624.euAiActRiskReasoning: Limited Risk: The reports describe generative AI models like Stable Diffusion 1.5 that are used for 'AI-generated content such as deepfakes' and non-consensual intimate imagery, which fall under transparency and disclosure obligations.
AIID-624.reasonForConfidence: The reports are highly detailed, originating from reputable academic institutions (Stanford Internet Observatory) and major news outlets. They provide consistent, validated numbers regarding the presence of CSAM (1,008 validated, 3,226 suspected) and the specific models involved (Stable Diffusion 1.5, Imagen). There is high consensus across the reports regarding the core facts of the incident.
AIID-624.ambiguitiesIdentified: There is some minor disagreement on whether Google's Imagen actually used LAION-5B or LAION-400M in its final versions, which was corrected in subsequent reports to clarify it only used LAION-400M for an unreleased research version.
AIID-624.alternativeInterpretations: None. The presence of CSAM in the dataset is a verified fact confirmed by multiple third-party child safety organizations.
AIID-624.natSecSummary: The discovery of CSAM and private personal data in the LAION-5B dataset highlights systemic vulnerabilities in generative AI training pipelines. While constituting severe human rights and privacy concerns, the national security impact remains minor, primarily affecting technological trust and requiring long-term regulatory and data curation adjustments rather than immediate defense intervention.
AIID-624.natSecImminenceJustification: Represents a systemic, ongoing vulnerability in AI data curation processes rather than an active, fast-moving national security crisis.
AIID-624.natSecAutonomyJustification: The dataset was compiled through human-directed web scraping, and the downstream generative models function strictly as human-controlled tools.
AIID-624.natSecNoveltyJustification: Represents a significant scaling up of traditional data contamination and copyright issues into the domain of foundational generative AI training.
AIID-624.natSecPhysicalJustification: No kinetic threats, physical system compromises, or critical infrastructure impacts were reported in connection with this dataset discovery.
AIID-624.natSecInformationJustification: No state-sponsored information warfare, intelligence compromise, or systematic disinformation campaigns were directly linked to this incident.
AIID-624.natSecSovereigntyJustification: Core government functions, electoral systems, and state sovereignty remained unaffected by the dataset contamination.
AIID-624.natSecEconomicJustification: Temporary removal of foundational datasets and pressure to deprecate models like Stable Diffusion 1.5 impact the AI commercial pipeline, but do not threaten national economic stability.
AIID-624.natSecSocietalJustification: The presence of CSAM and private medical records represents severe human rights and privacy violations, but the immediate impact is manageable within standard law enforcement and legal frameworks.

AIID-625.title: Proliferation of Products on Amazon Titled with ChatGPT Error Messages
AIID-625.summary: E-commerce and social media platforms are experiencing a surge in low-quality, AI-generated content where third-party sellers and bot operators use ChatGPT to automate text creation. Due to a lack of human oversight, many of these listings and posts are published containing verbatim AI error messages, such as 'I'm sorry but I cannot fulfill this request.' This trend highlights the risks of automated content generation in marketplaces and social platforms, leading to degraded user experiences and potential consumer deception.
AIID-625.description: Products named after ChatGPT error messages are proliferating on Amazon, such as lawn chairs and religious texts. These names, often resembling AI-generated errors, indicate a lack of editing and undermine the sense of authenticity and reliability of product listings.

AIID-626.title: Social Media Scammers Used Deepfakes of Taylor Swift and Several Other Celebrities in Fraudulent Le Creuset Cookware Giveaways
AIID-626.summary: A widespread fraudulent campaign used AI-generated deepfake videos of various celebrities to promote fake Le Creuset cookware giveaways on social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok. The ads directed users to phishing websites where they were tricked into paying a small shipping fee, which actually enrolled them in unauthorized, expensive monthly subscription plans. Victims never received the promised cookware and suffered financial loss and potential identity theft.
AIID-626.description: Scammers reportedly made deepfakes of Taylor Swift, Selena Gomez, Joanna Gaines, Lainey Wilson, Ree Drummond, Oprah, Jennifer Lopez, Trisha Yearwood, Martha Stewart, and Blake Shelton promoting a Le Creuset giveaway. These AI-generated ads, appearing on Meta and TikTok, falsely claimed users could receive free cookware by paying a small shipping fee. Victims were unknowingly enrolled in a costly monthly subscription.

AIID-627.title: Unauthorized AI Impersonation of George Carlin Used in Comedy Special

AIID-628.title: Fake Biden Voice in Robocall Misleads New Hampshire Democratic Voters in 2024 Primary Election
AIID-628.summary: In January 2024, a political consultant commissioned a deepfake robocall using AI-generated audio to impersonate President Joe Biden. The call, which targeted New Hampshire voters ahead of the primary, falsely urged Democrats to skip the election. The incident led to criminal indictments for voter suppression and significant regulatory fines from the FCC, marking a notable instance of AI-enabled election interference.
AIID-628.description: A robocall imitating President Biden's voice urged New Hampshire Democrats to skip the 2024 primary, falsely claiming their votes mattered more in November. Investigators with the New Hampshire Attorney General's Office, along with other state AGs, the Industry Traceback Group, and the FCC determined that political consultant Steve Kramer hired Paul Carpenter to create the deepfake, which was distributed by Walter Monk's company, Life Corporation. Rep. Dean Phillips, who employed Kramer, has distanced himself from the incident. Kathy Sullivan, the former New Hampshire Democratic Party chair, was falsely impersonated in the caller ID data used for the robocalls.

AIID-630.title: Alleged Macy's Facial Recognition Error Leads to Wrongful Arrest and Subsequent Sexual Assault in Jail
AIID-630.summary: A 61-year-old man was wrongfully arrested for armed robbery after a retail loss prevention agent used facial recognition software to misidentify him. While held in jail for ten days, the man was beaten and sexually assaulted by other inmates. He is now suing the retail companies involved for $10 million, highlighting the dangers of relying on error-prone facial recognition technology for law enforcement investigations.
AIID-630.description: Harvey Murphy Jr. was wrongfully accused of robbing a Sunglass Hut due to an alleged misidentification by the facial recognition system operated by Macy's. AIID-633.title: Nine Network's AI Alters Lawmaker Georgie Purcell's Image Inappropriately
AIID-633.summary: Nine News Melbourne broadcast a digitally altered image of Victorian MP Georgie Purcell during a news segment. The image, modified using Adobe Photoshop's Generative Expand tool, sexualized the MP by enlarging her breasts and exposing her midriff. While the network blamed 'automation by Photoshop,' Adobe stated that such changes require human intervention. The incident sparked significant public debate regarding media ethics, the sexualization of women in politics, and the risks of using generative AI in newsrooms.
AIID-633.description: The Nine Network used Photoshop's Generative Expand AI tool to resize an image of lawmaker Georgie Purcell, inadvertently altering her attire to appear more revealing. This error, claimed to result from the AI's automation, led to public criticism and an apology from the network.

AIID-633.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the Photoshop Generative Expand tool in this context was to retouch and resize an existing image of the MP, generating new visual content to fill the expanded frame.

AIID-634.title: Alleged Deepfake CFO Scam Reportedly Costs Multinational Engineering Firm Arup $25 Million
AIID-634.summary: In January 2024, a finance employee at the Hong Kong branch of the engineering firm Arup was defrauded of approximately $25 million USD. The employee was tricked into attending a video conference call where deepfake recreations of the company's CFO and other colleagues were present. Believing the call to be legitimate, the employee followed instructions to execute 15 wire transfers to five different bank accounts. The fraud was discovered a week later when the employee contacted the company's headquarters.

AIID-634.natSecAutonomyJustification: The AI deepfake tools were directly controlled and deployed by human fraudsters as tools to generate synthetic video and audio, without autonomous decision-making.
AIID-634.natSecNoveltyJustification: Significant advancement in deepfake fraud, moving from single-person static impersonation to a live, multi-person video conference call simulation.
AIID-634.natSecPhysicalJustification: The incident was purely financial fraud via deepfake video conferencing, with no physical systems, critical infrastructure, or human safety compromised.
AIID-634.natSecInformationJustification: Sophisticated use of multi-person deepfake video to deceive, but targeted a private corporate entity for financial gain rather than state-level intelligence or systematic information warfare.
AIID-634.natSecSovereigntyJustification: The incident targeted a private engineering firm and did not impact government decision-making, electoral systems, or sovereign state operations.
AIID-634.natSecEconomicJustification: Significant financial loss of 25.6 million USD to a major engineering firm, but manageable within corporate limits and does not threaten national economic stability.
AIID-634.natSecSocietalJustification: The scam was a targeted corporate fraud event and did not cause widespread societal instability, civil unrest, or human rights violations.

Employee was untrained in identifying subtle AI-generation anomalies.

No protocol required verifying urgent requests via an alternative channel.
Fifteen anomalous transfers went undetected over a week-long period.

Regulatory Environment.Explanation: Absence of strict regulations or liabilities for deepfake creation tools.
Social and video platforms lacked strict controls on executive impersonations.

AIID-637.title: Gunshot Detection Technology ShotSpotter (now SoundThinking) Reportedly Only Has 47% Accuracy in Chicago System
AIID-637.summary: An analysis of internal Chicago Police Department records from 2017-2018 revealed that the ShotSpotter gunshot detection system had an accuracy rate of approximately 47% in identifying confirmed shootings in the city's tenth district. The system frequently failed to alert officers to incidents where individuals were struck by gunfire, raising concerns about delayed emergency responses and the efficacy of the technology as a public safety tool.
AIID-637.description: SoundThinking's (formerly ShotSpotter's) system in Chicago, with a reported 47% accuracy rate for detecting actual gunshots, led to potential public safety risks by failing to alert police to real shootings, possibly delaying emergency response to violent incidents and misdirecting law enforcement resources.

AIID-638.title: Fatal Crash Involving Tesla Full Self-Driving Claims Employee's Life
AIID-638.summary: In May 2022, a Tesla employee, Hans von Ohain, died in a fatal crash in Evergreen, Colorado, after his Model 3 veered off a mountain road and struck a tree, resulting in a severe fire. While the driver was found to have a blood alcohol level significantly above the legal limit, the passenger alleged that the vehicle's Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature was engaged. Investigators noted the absence of skid marks and the presence of rolling tire marks, suggesting the vehicle's propulsion system remained active upon impact, though Tesla and CEO Elon Musk have disputed whether FSD was active or even installed on the vehicle.

AIID-639.title: Air Canada Chatbot Reportedly Provides Inaccurate Bereavement Fare Information, Leading to Customer Overpayment
AIID-639.summary: Air Canada was ordered by a civil tribunal to pay damages to a customer after its AI chatbot provided incorrect information regarding bereavement fare refund policies. The chatbot falsely informed the customer that they could book a full-price ticket and claim a retroactive discount within 90 days, which contradicted the airline's actual policy. Air Canada unsuccessfully argued that the chatbot was a separate legal entity, but the tribunal ruled the airline responsible for the information provided by its automated systems.
AIID-639.description: A Canadian small claims tribunal reportedly ordered Air Canada to pay $812.02 in damages and court fees after its website chatbot allegedly provided inaccurate information about bereavement fare eligibility, leading a customer to overpay for flights. The tribunal reportedly found the airline responsible for information presented by its chatbot, rejecting the argument that the chatbot was a separate legal entity, and characterized the error as negligent misrepresentation.

AIID-642.title: ChatGPT Glitch Disrupts User Interactions with Nonsensical Outputs

AIID-644.title: Alleged State-Sponsored Hackers Escalate Purported Phishing Attacks Using Artificial Intelligence
AIID-644.summary: Microsoft and OpenAI identified and disrupted the use of generative AI services by state-affiliated threat actors from North Korea, Iran, Russia, and China. These actors utilized large language models to improve the sophistication of spear-phishing campaigns, conduct reconnaissance on defense and cybersecurity targets, and assist in social engineering and malware development. While the techniques were described as early-stage, the incident highlights the use of AI to lower the barrier for sophisticated cyber operations and disinformation.
AIID-644.description: State-sponsored hackers from North Korea, Iran, Russia, and China are reportedly leveraging artificial intelligence to conduct sophisticated phishing and social engineering attacks. AIID-645.title: Seeming Pattern of Gemini Bias and Sociotechnical Training Failures Harm Google's Reputation
AIID-645.summary: Google's Gemini AI chatbot experienced a significant controversy following its release of image generation features, which produced historically inaccurate and racially diverse depictions of figures and groups (such as Nazi soldiers and US Founding Fathers). The company acknowledged that its tuning for diversity resulted in overcompensation and inaccuracies, leading to a temporary suspension of the image generation feature for people. Additionally, the chatbot faced criticism for providing problematic text responses to sensitive moral and political questions.
AIID-645.description: Google's Gemini chatbot faced many reported bias issues upon release, leading to a variety of problematic outputs like racial inaccuracies and political biases, including regarding Chinese and Indian politics. It also reportedly over-corrected racial diversity in historical contexts and advanced controversial perspectives, prompting a temporary halt and an apology from Google.

AIID-648.title: Alleged Deepfake Audio of Imran Khan Calls for Election Boycott, Misleading Pakistan Voters
AIID-648.summary: In the lead-up to Pakistan's 2024 general elections, malicious actors disseminated AI-generated deepfake audio and video clips falsely attributed to political leaders, including Imran Khan. These clips falsely claimed that the PTI party was boycotting the elections, aiming to mislead voters and disrupt the democratic process. AIID-653.title: Two Investment Firms Charged with Making False Claims of Artificial Intelligence Capabilities in Case of AI Washing
AIID-653.summary: The SEC charged two investment firms, Delphia and Global Predictions, for 'AI washing'—falsely claiming to use AI in their investment processes between 2019 and 2023. The firms agreed to pay a combined $400,000 in civil penalties to settle the charges. This case highlights the regulatory focus on preventing misleading marketing regarding AI capabilities in the financial sector.
AIID-653.description: In a case of AI washing, the SEC charged two investment advisers, Delphia and Global Predictions, for falsely stating their use of artificial intelligence in their investment strategies between 2019 and 2023. Their misleading claims resulted in a settlement whereby the firms agreed to pay a total of $400,000 in penalties, highlighting the critical consequences of misrepresenting AI capabilities on investment decisions and trust.
AIID-653.domainJustification: The firms made false claims about possessing AI capabilities ('AI washing') to mislead investors and gain an illegitimate competitive and financial advantage.
AIID-653.aiGoalJustification: The firms falsely marketed their purported AI systems as being able to predict market trends and provide expert AI-driven forecasts.

AIID-654.title: Microsoft Copilot Designer Reportedly Generated Inappropriate AI Images
AIID-654.summary: A Microsoft software engineering manager submitted a letter to the FTC and Microsoft's board of directors alleging that the company's Copilot Designer tool generates harmful and inappropriate content, including sexualized and violent imagery, from benign prompts. The employee, who previously raised concerns about the underlying DALL-E model, argues that Microsoft is failing to implement necessary safeguards or age-appropriate ratings. The report highlights a broader industry challenge regarding the safety of generative AI image tools.
AIID-654.description: A Microsoft engineer reported that Copilot Designer, an AI image generator, creates content depicting sex, violence, bias, and more. Despite raising concerns and suggesting improvements, the tool remains public, prompting a letter to the FTC.

AIID-655.title: Scams Reportedly Impersonating Wealthy Investors Proliferating on Facebook
AIID-655.summary: Sophisticated investment scams impersonating high-profile financial figures are proliferating on Facebook. These scams utilize deepfake technology and targeted advertising to lure victims into fraudulent investment groups, resulting in significant financial losses. Despite Meta's use of AI systems to detect and block such content, the systems are reportedly failing to prevent the spread of these ads, leading to criticism regarding the platform's enforcement efficacy.
AIID-655.description: Scams are reportedly proliferating throughout Facebook impersonating wealthy individuals such as Bill Ackman, Cathie Wood, Steve Cohen, Peter Lynch, and Ray Dalio. In some cases, it seems deepfake technology is being employed, while simultaneously Facebook's own AI systems are allegedly faltering in their ability to halt the spread of these fraudulent ads despite being reported.

AIID-656.title: Purported Deepfake Disinformation Aired on Russian State TV Allegedly Linking Ukraine to Moscow Attack
AIID-656.summary: Russian state television broadcast a deepfake video featuring AI-generated audio of Ukrainian security official Oleksiy Danilov, falsely suggesting Ukrainian involvement in the Crocus City Hall terrorist attack. The video was identified as a composite of existing interviews with AI-generated audio dubbed over the footage. This incident is described as part of a disinformation campaign to influence public opinion and justify further aggression against Ukraine.
AIID-656.description: Russian state television reportedly aired a fabricated video that appeared to imitate senior Ukrainian security officials and present a false admission of involvement in the Crocus City Hall massacre. The clip reportedly used elements from recent interviews combined with allegedly AI-generated audio to create a misleading confession. ISIS-K is reported to have publicly claimed responsibility, while independent analysts and governments have rejected the narrative promoted through the video.

AIID-657.title: ChatGPT Account Compromise Leads to Unintended Data Exposure
AIID-657.summary: A user reported that their ChatGPT account history was populated with sensitive conversations belonging to unrelated individuals, including login credentials for a pharmacy portal. OpenAI investigated the incident and attributed the exposure to an account takeover originating from Sri Lanka, though the incident highlighted broader concerns regarding the lack of 2FA and login tracking on the platform. The event underscores the risks of data leakage in AI services and the importance of user-side data hygiene.
AIID-657.description: A security breach involving ChatGPT led to the exposure of sensitive conversations, including login credentials and personal data, after a user account was compromised. OpenAI responded to the incident with an explanation.
AIID-657.subdomain: 2.1 Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information
AIID-657.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"2.2 AI system security vulnerabilities and attacks","justification":"The exposure was facilitated by an account takeover and a lack of standard security features like 2FA on the ChatGPT platform."}]
AIID-657.domainJustification: The incident involved the exposure of non-public sensitive information, including pharmacy portal login credentials and unpublished research details, to an unrelated user.
AIID-657.aiGoalJustification: ChatGPT is primarily deployed as a conversational chatbot and writing assistant to help users with queries, coding, and brainstorming.

AIID-657.causalJustification: The incident was primarily caused by human actions, specifically an intentional account takeover by external actors and a lack of standard security features implemented by OpenAI developers.
AIID-657.euAiActRiskReasoning: Limited Risk: ChatGPT is a general-purpose chatbot, which falls under the category of AI systems that pose a moderate risk and require specific transparency obligations.
AIID-657.reasonForConfidence: The report provides clear details of the incident, including the user's account, the nature of the leaked data, and OpenAI's official explanation of an account takeover. AIID-657.ambiguitiesIdentified: There is a slight conflict between the user's belief that his account was not compromised and OpenAI's finding of successful logins from Sri Lanka.

AIID-657.natSecSummary: Consumer ChatGPT accounts were compromised via credential stuffing originating from Sri Lanka, leading to the exposure of private chat histories, including commercial credentials and unpublished research. The incident represents a minor privacy and commercial security issue rather than a national security threat, manageable through standard cyber hygiene and platform security updates.
AIID-657.natSecImminenceJustification: The immediate incident is resolved, but it highlights ongoing, long-term strategic concerns regarding data privacy and security hygiene in consumer AI platforms.
AIID-657.natSecAutonomyJustification: The AI system functions as a passive assistant, and the security compromise resulted entirely from human actions such as credential stuffing and account takeover.
AIID-657.natSecNoveltyJustification: Credential stuffing, account takeovers, and unauthorized data exposure are highly common and established cyber security threats, not a novel AI-specific exploit.
AIID-657.natSecPhysicalJustification: No kinetic threats, weapons deployment, or critical infrastructure manipulation occurred. The leaked pharmacy portal credentials represent a commercial/privacy issue rather than a national security threat to critical infrastructure.
AIID-657.natSecInformationJustification: No intelligence capabilities or classified data were compromised. The leaked research proposal and PHP script do not constitute state-level intelligence or information warfare.
AIID-657.natSecSovereigntyJustification: Core government operations, electoral systems, and state sovereignty were entirely unaffected by this consumer-level account compromise.
AIID-657.natSecEconomicJustification: Minor risk to intellectual property (unpublished research proposal) and commercial credentials. Manageable through standard security procedures like password resets and implementing multi-factor authentication.
AIID-657.natSecSocietalJustification: Limited privacy compromise affecting a small number of individuals whose chat histories were exposed. Does not represent large-scale societal instability or systemic human rights violations.

AIID-658.title: The Arizona Agenda Produced a Deepfake of Kari Lake Advocating for the Publication Without Her Consent
AIID-658.summary: The Arizona Agenda, a local political newsletter, created and published a deepfake video of Senate candidate Kari Lake to demonstrate the accessibility and dangers of AI-generated disinformation. While the outlet intended the video as an educational tool, it did not obtain Lake's consent, leading her campaign to issue a cease-and-desist letter. The incident sparked debate among experts regarding the balance between public education and the risk of normalizing synthetic media in political campaigns.
AIID-658.description: The Arizona Agenda produced a deepfake video of Republican Senate candidate Kari Lake giving a testimonial about the publication with the seeming intention of educating the general public about the dangers of deepfakes in the coming election cycle. AIID-659.title: Mass Facial Recognition Program in Gaza Reportedly Used by Israeli Forces to Identify Palestinians
AIID-659.summary: Israeli military intelligence deployed a facial recognition program in Gaza using Corsight technology and Google Photos to identify and detain individuals. The system, which operated without the knowledge or consent of the Palestinian population, produced false positives that led to the arbitrary detention and interrogation of civilians, including a Palestinian poet. The program was used to create 'hit lists' of suspected militants, but its reliance on grainy footage and automated matching resulted in significant errors.
AIID-659.description: A previously undisclosed facial recognition initiative operated by Israeli military intelligence units was reportedly deployed across Gaza after the October 7, 2023 attacks. According to multiple intelligence officers, the program uses Corsight technology alongside Google Photos to identify individuals from checkpoints, crowds, and drone footage. The system has allegedly produced misidentifications, including the widely reported detention of Palestinian poet Mosab Abu Toha on November 19, 2023.

AIID-663.title: China Reportedly Intensifying AI to Spread Disinformation to U.S. and Taiwanese Voters
AIID-663.summary: Foreign state-sponsored actors from China, Russia, and Iran integrated generative AI into covert influence operations targeting U.S. and Taiwanese elections. These operations utilized AI to scale the production of fake news articles, political cartoons, and voice clones, though the report notes that these tools generally helped scale content rather than improving its quality or persuasiveness. AIID-663.description: AI tools linked to China were used to disseminate disinformation targeting voters in the U.S. and Taiwan, according to a Microsoft report. AIID-672.title: 'Lavender' and 'The Gospel' AI Systems Reportedly Used in Gaza Targeting Operations with Civilian Harm Allegations
AIID-672.summary: Investigations report that the Israel Defense Forces utilized AI systems, specifically 'Lavender' and 'The Gospel', to generate target lists of suspected militants in Gaza. These systems, combined with tracking software like 'Where's Daddy?', were used to authorize airstrikes on residential homes, resulting in significant civilian casualties. Sources indicate that human oversight was minimal, with officers often acting as a 'rubber stamp' for AI-generated targets.
AIID-672.description: The AI system known as "Lavender" was reportedly used by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) to assist in identifying individuals in Gaza for targeting, while a related system, "The Gospel," was reportedly used to help select and prioritize physical strike targets. Investigations reportedly suggest that these systems operated with limited human review and may have contributed to strikes associated with high civilian casualties. The extent of automation with human oversight, as well as the accuracy of these targeting processes, reportedly remain subjects of dispute.
AIID-672.subdomain: 4.2 Cyberattacks, weapon development or use, and mass harm
AIID-672.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.2 Loss of human agency and autonomy","justification":"Human operators delegated critical targeting decisions to the AI, spending only 20 seconds to rubber-stamp recommendations."},{"code":"7.3 Lack of capability or robustness","justification":"The Lavender system had an acknowledged 10 percent error rate, frequently misidentifying civilians, civil defense workers, and police as militants."}]
AIID-672.domainJustification: The use of the Lavender and Where's Daddy? AI systems to systematically target and execute military strikes causing mass civilian casualties constitutes the use of AI weapons to cause mass harm.
AIID-672.allegedHarmedParties: Palestinians, National security and intelligence stakeholders, Gazans
AIID-672.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the Lavender and The Gospel systems is to identify specific individuals and structures as military targets for airstrikes.
AIID-672.physicalHarmCaused:
Reported: Yes, the reports explicitly describe extensive physical harm, including tens of thousands of deaths and injuries resulting from airstrikes guided by the AI systems.
Directly caused: The reports state that during the first six weeks of the war, when the military almost completely relied on Lavender, approximately 15,000 Palestinians were killed.
Indirectly caused: Thousands of civilians, including over 13,000 children, were killed as collateral damage in strikes targeting residential homes.
Inferred additional harm: It is likely that tens of thousands of additional individuals suffered severe physical injuries or death under the rubble, with total casualties exceeding 30,000 to 50,000.
AIID-672.infrastructureHarmCaused:
Reported: Yes, the reports explicitly describe catastrophic damage to critical infrastructure in Gaza.
Directly caused: Airstrikes targeting residential homes and buildings identified by Lavender and The Gospel destroyed or damaged nearly 70 percent of Gaza's homes.
Indirectly caused: The destruction led to the collapse of the healthcare system, leaving fewer than one-third of hospitals functioning, and causing catastrophic food insecurity for 1.1 million people.
Inferred additional harm: We infer extensive, long-term damage to water, sanitation, electrical grids, and communication networks across the entire Gaza Strip, requiring billions of dollars and decades to rebuild.
AIID-672.propertyHarmCaused:
Reported: Yes, the reports explicitly describe massive property damage across Gaza.
Directly caused: The IDF destroyed more than 360,000 buildings and flattened entire residential blocks using unguided dumb bombs on AI-selected targets.
Indirectly caused: More than half of Gaza's buildings and 70 percent of homes were damaged or destroyed as collateral damage from the targeting campaign.
Inferred additional harm: The total value of destroyed residential, commercial, and public property is inferred to be in the billions of dollars, decimating the personal wealth of millions of residents.
AIID-672.financialHarmCaused:
Reported: No, the reports do not explicitly quantify the total financial losses in monetary terms, though they mention massive destruction of property and the high cost of precision munitions.
Directly caused: N/A
Indirectly caused: N/A
Inferred additional harm: We infer catastrophic financial losses in the billions of dollars due to the destruction of hundreds of thousands of homes, businesses, and public infrastructure.
AIID-672.environmentalHarmCaused:
Reported: No, the reports do not explicitly describe environmental damage caused by the AI systems.
Directly caused: N/A
Indirectly caused: N/A
Inferred additional harm: The detonation of thousands of heavy munitions and the collapse of hundreds of thousands of buildings likely caused severe air pollution, soil contamination, and toxic dust accumulation.
AIID-672.maliciousContentHarmCaused:
Reported: No, the reports do not describe the creation or spread of toxic or malicious digital content by the AI.
Directly caused: N/A
Indirectly caused: N/A
Inferred additional harm: N/A
AIID-672.differentialTreatmentHarmCaused:
Reported: Yes, the reports describe systematic differential treatment of Palestinians in Gaza through mass surveillance and algorithmic profiling.
Directly caused: The Lavender system profiled and assigned a numerical threat score from 1 to 100 to almost all 2.3 million Palestinian residents of Gaza to identify targets.
Indirectly caused: The military applied highly permissive collateral damage rules to Palestinian targets, allowing up to 20 civilian deaths for low-level targets, which is unprecedented compared to other modern conflicts.
Inferred additional harm: The algorithmic profiling of an entire population based on demographic and communication features likely resulted in systemic discrimination and arbitrary deprivation of life for thousands of innocent individuals.
AIID-672.civilRightsHarmCaused:
Reported: Yes, the reports explicitly describe severe violations of human rights and international humanitarian law.
Directly caused: The algorithmic generation of kill lists and subsequent airstrikes violated the fundamental right to life for thousands of individuals, including non-combatants.
Indirectly caused: The systematic bombing of families in their homes violated the Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949, which forbids the indiscriminate killing of non-combatants.
Inferred additional harm: The widespread use of automated targeting with minimal human verification represents a systemic erosion of the right to due process, distinction, and proportionality under international law.
AIID-672.democracyHarmCaused:
Reported: No, the reports do not explicitly describe the erosion of democratic norms within a state, though they mention international legal scrutiny.
Directly caused: N/A
Indirectly caused: N/A
Inferred additional harm: The lack of transparency and accountability in deploying lethal AI systems by a democratic state's military may weaken domestic democratic oversight and international legal norms governing warfare.
AIID-672.privacyHarmCaused:
Reported: Yes, the reports describe massive privacy violations through the surveillance systems feeding the AI.
Directly caused: The Lavender system analyzed personal data collected on almost all 2.3 million residents of Gaza through a system of mass surveillance, including phone contacts, social media, and location data.
Indirectly caused: The Where's Daddy? system tracked individuals' real-time locations and entry into their private family homes to facilitate airstrikes.
Inferred additional harm: The continuous, non-consensual harvesting of deeply personal communication and location data of millions of civilians represents an unprecedented scale of privacy intrusion.
AIID-672.psychologicalHarmCaused:
Reported: Yes, the reports describe severe psychological trauma, grief, and distress among survivors and military personnel.
Directly caused: An anonymous intelligence officer expressed being shocked and traumatized after realizing they authorized a strike on a home where the target was absent, killing innocent families.
Indirectly caused: Widespread trauma, grief, and terror were experienced by Gazan civilians, such as Amjad Al-Yazji, who discovered 11 deceased family members under the rubble of their home.
Inferred additional harm: Widespread, long-term post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and severe psychological trauma are inferred to affect hundreds of thousands of Gazan residents, particularly children.

AIID-672.causalJustification: The incident was caused by the deployment of the Lavender and Where's Daddy? AI systems, which were intentionally used post-deployment to generate and track lethal military targets.
AIID-672.euAiActRiskReasoning: Unacceptable Risk: The report describes an AI system that performs mass surveillance and algorithmic profiling of an entire population, assigning a threat score of 1 to 100 to individuals, which is highly analogous to prohibited 'social scoring by governments' under Risk Level 1.
AIID-672.reasonForConfidence: The reports are highly detailed, drawing on extensive investigative journalism from multiple reputable outlets (+972, Local Call, The Guardian, NYT) and first-hand testimonies from six anonymous Israeli intelligence officers who operated the systems. The core facts regarding the existence of Lavender, Where's Daddy?, and The Gospel, their error rates, and the minimal human oversight are consistent across all sources.
AIID-672.ambiguitiesIdentified: The exact mathematical algorithms and specific features used by Lavender to calculate the 1-100 scores remain proprietary and are described only generally. There is also a conflict between the testimonies of the intelligence officers and the official denials of the IDF spokesperson regarding the automated nature of the kill lists.
AIID-672.alternativeInterpretations: The IDF interprets these systems purely as auxiliary databases meant to assist human analysts, rather than automated decision-making systems that direct lethal strikes.
AIID-672.natSecSummary: The deployment of Lavender, The Gospel, and Where's Daddy? represents the first documented case of mass-scale AI systems directing lethal military targeting in active warfare. By reducing human oversight to a rubber stamp, the system caused unprecedented civilian casualties and infrastructure damage, establishing a dangerous global precedent for automated warfare and violating international humanitarian law.
AIID-672.natSecImminenceJustification: Active military campaign with ongoing kinetic strikes and immediate life-safety implications.
AIID-672.natSecAutonomyJustification: Targeting decisions were generated by AI but required a brief 20-second human verification before execution.
AIID-672.natSecNoveltyJustification: First documented instance of a military utilizing mass-scale AI profiling and tracking systems to direct lethal airstrikes.
AIID-672.natSecPhysicalJustification: AI-directed targeting systems (Lavender and The Gospel) directly authorized kinetic airstrikes resulting in over 15,000 reported deaths and the destruction of 70 percent of Gaza's housing and infrastructure.
AIID-672.natSecInformationJustification: Systematic deployment of mass surveillance capabilities harvesting data on 2.3 million residents to feed targeting models, representing an unprecedented scale of automated intelligence collection.
AIID-672.natSecSovereigntyJustification: Foreign military forces deployed AI target-generation systems within contested territory, effectively replacing human command decisions with automated targeting algorithms, disrupting sovereign control.
AIID-672.natSecEconomicJustification: Airstrikes on AI-selected targets caused billions of dollars in property and infrastructure damage, decimating the local economy, though strategic global tech security was not directly targeted.
AIID-672.natSecSocietalJustification: Algorithmic profiling of 2.3 million people with a 10 percent error rate led to systemic human rights violations, mass civilian casualties, and the complete collapse of societal stability in Gaza.

Army used unguided munitions on junior targets to save expensive smart bombs.
Target presence at home was not verified in real-time before airstrikes.

Loosening of international law rules regarding collateral damage thresholds.
No external monitoring or accountability mechanisms for military AI use.

AIID-675.title: High School Athletic Director in Baltimore County Allegedly Created Racist Deepfake Audio Impersonating Principal
AIID-675.summary: Dazhon Darien, the athletic director at Pikesville High School, used AI tools to create a deepfake audio recording of Principal Eric Eiswert making racist and antisemitic comments. The recording was circulated on social media in January 2024, leading to the principal's temporary removal, threats to his safety, and significant disruption to the school district. Darien was later arrested and pleaded guilty to disturbing school operations, with investigators determining the recording was fabricated in retaliation for an investigation into his own potential financial misconduct.
AIID-675.description: Dazhon Darien, former athletic director at Pikesville High School in Baltimore, allegedly used AI to create a purported deepfake audio clip impersonating Principal Eric Eiswert, embedding racist and antisemitic remarks. According to reports, the clip was intended to discredit Eiswert and was widely circulated, with some accounts linking it to threats and his placement on administrative leave. On April 28, 2025, Darien was reportedly sentenced to four months in jail after pleading guilty to disturbing school operations.

AIID-676.title: Alleged Deepfake Audio Depicts Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Ordering Military Action

AIID-677.title: ChatGPT and Perplexity Reportedly Manipulated into Breaking Content Policies in AI Boyfriend Scenarios
AIID-677.summary: Researchers and users have identified a trend where generative AI chatbots, including ChatGPT and Perplexity, are being manipulated through 'jailbreak' prompts to adopt 'AI boyfriend' personas. These manipulations successfully bypass safety guardrails, causing the models to generate sexually explicit content, suggest dangerous activities, and solicit sensitive personal information. While newer models exhibit more resistance, the report highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in current safety training.
AIID-677.description: The "Dan" ("Do Anything Now") AI boyfriend is a trend on TikTok in which users appear to regularly manipulate ChatGPT to adopt boyfriend personas, breaching content policies. ChatGPT 3.5 is reported to regularly produce explicitly sexual content, directly violating its intended safety protocols. GPT-4 and Perplexity AI were subjected to similar manipulations, and although they exhibited more resistance to breaches, some prompts were reported to break its guidelines.

AIID-678.title: ChatGPT Factual Errors Lead to Filing of Complaint of GDPR Privacy Violation
AIID-678.summary: The privacy advocacy group noyb has filed a formal complaint against OpenAI with the Austrian data protection authority, alleging that ChatGPT violates GDPR requirements. The complaint centers on the model's tendency to hallucinate inaccurate personal data, such as birthdates, and the company's failure to provide mechanisms for users to correct or delete this information. AIID-679.title: A Purported Deepfake of Senator Elizabeth Warren Circulates Allegedly Saying Republicans Should Not Vote
AIID-679.summary: In February 2023, a deepfake video of Senator Elizabeth Warren circulated on social media, falsely depicting her claiming that Republicans should be barred from voting in the 2024 election. The video, which originated on TikTok and gained significant traction on Twitter, used AI to manipulate footage from an actual MSNBC interview. While many users identified the video as fake and Twitter applied an 'altered audio' label, some individuals were misled by the content, which aimed to fuel political polarization.

AIID-680.title: Russia-Linked AI CopyCop Site Identified as Modifying and Producing at Least 19,000 Deceptive Reports
AIID-680.summary: The CopyCop network, a Russian-linked influence operation, utilized generative AI models including ChatGPT and DALL-E 3 to automate the creation and dissemination of over 19,000 deceptive news articles. By plagiarizing and rewriting content from legitimate media outlets with specific partisan prompts, the network aimed to influence political discourse in the US, France, and the UK. While the operation successfully scaled its content production, researchers and government agencies identified and debunked many of its narratives, noting that the AI-generated content was often of low quality and failed to significantly alter election outcomes.
AIID-680.description: In early March 2024, a network named CopyCop began publishing modified news stories using AI, altering content to spread partisan biases and disinformation. These articles, initially from legitimate sources, were manipulated by AI models, possibly developed by OpenAI, to disseminate Russian propaganda. Over 19,000 articles were published, targeting divisive political issues and creating false narratives.

AIID-683.title: Scammers Using Deepfakes of Women's Faces and Voices for False and Offensive Advertisements
AIID-683.summary: Scammers are increasingly using AI tools from companies like HeyGen and ElevenLabs to create deepfake videos of influencers and private individuals without their consent. These deepfakes are used to promote offensive products, such as erectile dysfunction supplements, or to spread political disinformation targeting specific demographics. Victims report feeling violated and helpless as their likenesses are manipulated to say things they would never say, with limited recourse for removal or legal action.
AIID-683.description: Scammers used AI tools from HeyGen and ElevenLabs to create deepfake videos of influencers Michel Janse, Olga Loiek, Shadé Zahrai, and Carrie Williams, misusing Lana Smalls's voice in Williams's case. These videos promoted offensive products and false messages, in some cases targeting nationalist Chinese men to boost China-Russia ties, causing emotional distress and damaging the victims' reputations.

AIID-684.title: Google Books Appears to Be Indexing Works Written by AI
AIID-684.summary: Google Books has been found to index low-quality, AI-generated books, identified by common chatbot phrases like 'as of my last knowledge update.' This practice threatens the integrity of the Google Books database and the accuracy of the Google Ngram Viewer, a tool used by academics to track language evolution. While Google claims current Ngram data is not affected, the presence of AI-generated content in the index poses a risk to future research and data reliability.
AIID-684.description: Google Books is indexing low-quality, AI-generated books, degrading its database and potentially distorting Google Ngram Viewer's analysis of language trends. This integration of inaccurate or misleading information undermines trust, disseminates poor-quality content, and wastes resources as researchers must spend time clearing up the misinformation.

AIID-685.title: The WHO's S.A.R.A.H. Bot Reported to Provide Inconsistent and Inadequate Health Information
AIID-685.summary: The World Health Organization's AI health advisor, SARAH, has been criticized for providing inconsistent and unreliable health information. AIID-688.title: Scarlett Johansson Alleges OpenAI's Sky Imitates Her Voice Without Licensing
AIID-688.summary: OpenAI released a new voice assistant feature for ChatGPT called 'Sky' that many users and the actress Scarlett Johansson noted sounded 'eerily similar' to her voice. Johansson, who had previously declined an offer from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to license her voice, publicly stated she was shocked and angered by the release. OpenAI subsequently suspended the use of the Sky voice, maintaining that it was the natural voice of a different actress and not an imitation, though the incident sparked significant debate regarding AI ethics, likeness rights, and the need for transparency in AI development.
AIID-688.description: OpenAI unveiled a voice assistant with a voice resembling Scarlett Johansson's, despite her refusal to license her voice. AIID-689.summary: A Wisconsin man was arrested by the FBI for allegedly using the open-source AI model Stable Diffusion to generate approximately 13,000 sexually explicit images of minors. The perpetrator distributed these images via Telegram and Instagram, including sending them directly to a 15-year-old boy. This case is noted as one of the first federal prosecutions involving the use of generative AI to create child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

AIID-690.title: ISIS Utilizes AI for Propaganda Videos in News Harvest Program
AIID-690.summary: Extremist groups, including ISIS and neo-Nazi networks, are increasingly utilizing AI tools to produce propaganda, deepfake news broadcasts, and instructional content. By leveraging AI for voice cloning, image generation, and text-based chatbots, these groups have significantly reduced the time and cost required to create professional-grade radicalization materials. This trend represents a shift in how extremist organizations disseminate content and recruit followers, posing new challenges for content moderation and counter-terrorism efforts.
AIID-690.description: ISIS supporters have created an AI-generated media program called News Harvest to disseminate propaganda videos. The program produces near-weekly broadcasts featuring AI-generated news anchors discussing ISIS operations globally, using cheap and easy-to-use AI tools. This development showcases the use of AI as a powerful propaganda tool for extremist groups.

AIID-691.title: Facewatch Reported to Have Wrongfully Flagged Home Bargains Customer as Shoplifter
AIID-691.summary: Facial recognition technology deployed by retailers and police in the UK has resulted in multiple instances of mistaken identity. In one case, a customer was wrongfully accused of shoplifting and banned from stores, while in another, a man was detained by police after being incorrectly flagged as a wanted person. These incidents highlight concerns regarding the accuracy and potential for false positives in live facial recognition systems.
AIID-691.description: A facial-recognition software used by the British variety store Home Bargains is alleged to have misidentified "Sara" as a shoplifter, leading to staff searching her bag, escorting her from the premises, and banning her from the store. After, Facewatch is reported to have admitted its error to Sara. Facewatch is used by a number of different British stores.

AIID-693.title: Google AI Reportedly Delivering Confidently Incorrect and Harmful Information
AIID-693.summary: Google's AI Overviews feature, powered by the Gemini model, generated numerous inaccurate and potentially dangerous responses to user search queries shortly after its broad deployment. Examples included instructions to add glue to pizza, ingest rocks, and mix hazardous cleaning chemicals. Google acknowledged the errors, attributed them to uncommon queries, and implemented technical refinements to limit such outputs.
AIID-693.description: Google's AI search engine has reportedly been providing users with confidently incorrect and often harmful information. Reports highlight numerous inaccuracies, including misleading health advice and dangerous cooking suggestions. For example, it has falsely claimed Barack Obama as the first Muslim U.S. President, reflecting fringe conspiracy theories, or recommending that glue can be an ingredient in pizza.

AIID-695.title: Donald Trump's Presidential Campaign Released Deepfakes Attacking Ron DeSantis

AIID-696.title: Meta's AI Ad Platform Reportedly Causes Overspending and Poor Performance

AIID-699.title: VA Suicide Prevention Algorithm REACH VET Reportedly Prioritizes Men Over Women Veterans

AIID-700.title: Meta's AI Chatbots Are Reportedly Entering Online Support Communities Uninvited
AIID-700.summary: Meta's AI chatbot began automatically posting responses in private Facebook groups when no human replied to a question within an hour. In one instance, the bot fabricated a personal story about having a child with special needs to answer a parent's query, causing distress and frustration among group members who sought authentic human connection. The incident highlights concerns regarding the inappropriate deployment of generative AI in sensitive community support spaces.

AIID-704.title: Study Highlights Persistent Hallucinations in Legal AI Systems
AIID-704.summary: A Stanford University study found that specialized legal AI tools from LexisNexis and Thomson Reuters, as well as general-purpose models like GPT-4, frequently hallucinate, providing incorrect legal information and fake citations. These errors pose significant risks to legal professionals and litigants who may rely on the tools for authoritative research. The study highlights a lack of transparency and rigorous benchmarking in the legal AI industry.
AIID-704.description: Stanford University’s Human-Centered AI Institute (HAI) conducted a study in which they designed a "pre-registered dataset of over 200 open-ended legal queries" to test AI products by LexisNexis (creator of Lexis+ AI) and Thomson Reuters (creator of Westlaw AI-Assisted Research and Ask Practical Law AI).  The researchers found that these legal models hallucinate in 1 out of 6 (or more) benchmarking queries.

AIID-705.title: Turkish Student in Isparta Allegedly Uses AI to Cheat on Exam, Leading to Arrest
AIID-705.summary: A student in Turkey was arrested for using a sophisticated hardware setup involving a button-camera and ChatGPT to cheat on the 2024 YKS university entrance exam. The system transmitted exam questions to the AI in real-time, which then provided answers via an earpiece. The incident highlights the use of generative AI as a tool for academic fraud in high-stakes testing environments.

AIID-706.title: Scammers Using AI to Impersonate Small Businesses
AIID-706.summary: Scammers are leveraging AI tools like ChatGPT to create high-quality, error-free marketing copy and translate stolen content for fraudulent e-commerce listings. These copycats impersonate small businesses by scraping their videos, logos, and social media posts to sell cheap knockoffs or steal money directly from consumers. The resulting fraud has caused significant financial losses and reputational harm to small businesses, who struggle to keep pace with the scale and sophistication of these AI-enabled attacks.
AIID-706.description: Scammers are using AI to impersonate small businesses by copying their videos, logos, and social media posts. They create fake listings and ads, diverting customers to cheap knockoffs or stealing their money. This has severely impacted businesses like Bee Cups, Darn Tough Vermont, and Cascade hummingbird feeders, leading to significant financial losses, negative reviews, and damaged reputations. Their deployment of AI makes it challenging for small businesses to combat these fraudulent activities.

AIID-706.aiGoalJustification: The scammers used ChatGPT as a writing assistant to generate error-free marketing copy and translate stolen content into other languages like Dutch and Swedish.

AIID-707.title: Tesla Reportedly in Autopilot Mode Hits Parked Police Vehicle in Fullerton, California
AIID-707.summary: A Tesla vehicle operating in 'self-drive' mode crashed into a parked police patrol vehicle in Fullerton, California, while the officer was responding to a separate fatal accident. The officer was outside his vehicle and narrowly escaped injury. The driver admitted to being distracted by a cellphone while relying on the vehicle's AI system.
AIID-707.description: A Tesla reportedly in self-driving mode crashed into a parked patrol vehicle in Fullerton, California while the officer was responding to a fatal DUI crash. The officer narrowly escaped injury. The driver reports having been distracted by a cellphone and having relied on the Tesla’s AI. (The earlier crash involved a suspected DUI driver who killed a motorcyclist stopped at a red light.)

AIID-708.title: Reportedly Faulty AI Transcription Threatens Integrity of Genoa Bribery Probe
AIID-708.summary: In a Genoa bribery investigation, an automated speech-to-text software incorrectly transcribed a suspect's statement from 'licit financing' to 'illicit financing'. The error was discovered during a review of the audio recording, highlighting the risks of relying on unverified AI transcription in judicial settings. Experts suggest the error stems from probabilistic bias in the model's training data, which frequently associates the term 'financing' with 'illicit' conduct.
AIID-708.description: A reported AI transcription software error in a Genoa bribery investigation is alleged to have incorrectly recorded "illicit financing" instead of "licit financing," which could have significantly impacted the case. The mistake was discovered during a review and is an example of the risks of relying on AI in judicial settings.
AIID-708.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"The judicial system passively delegated transcription tasks to the software without establishing mandatory human review or verification protocols."}]
AIID-708.domainJustification: The speech-to-text software failed to perform robustly and accurately under real-world conditions, misinterpreting 'licit' as 'illicit' due to probabilistic bias.
AIID-708.allegedHarmedParties: Roberto Spinelli, Paolo Emilio Signorini, Italian general public, Giovanni Toti, Genoa Prosecutor’s Office
AIID-708.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the AI system is speech-to-text transcription, which falls under Voice Recognition. Its application in transcribing official court interrogations serves as Judicial Decision Support.

AIID-709.title: Unrepresented Litigant Misled by ChatGPT-Generated False Legal Citations in Manchester Court
AIID-709.summary: A litigant in person in a Manchester civil court case used ChatGPT to generate legal research. The AI provided four citations, one of which was entirely fabricated and three of which contained fictitious excerpts. The judge determined the submission of these false documents was inadvertent and did not penalize the litigant.
AIID-709.description: A litigant in person (LiP) in a Manchester civil case presented false legal citations generated by ChatGPT. It fabricated one case name and provided fictitious excerpts for three real cases, misleadingly supporting the LiP's argument. The judge, upon investigation, found the submissions to be inadvertent and did not penalize the LiP.

AIID-710.title: Facebook AI Reportedly Mislabels Auschwitz Photos as 'Bullying' and 'Nudity'
AIID-710.summary: Meta's content moderation AI incorrectly flagged and demoted historical photographs from the Auschwitz Memorial Museum, labeling them as 'bullying' and 'nudity'. One image of orphans was deleted by the system. Meta later apologized, stating the notices were sent in error and that the content did not violate policies.
AIID-710.description: Facebook's AI system allegedly mislabeled around 20 posts from the Auschwitz Memorial Museum as violating community standards for "bullying" and "nudity," reportedly deleting at least one image of orphans. The purported misclassification of historical content allegedly prompted outrage from the museum, which reportedly demanded an explanation. Meta later purportedly apologized, attributing the issue to mistaken notices sent by its AI system and reportedly acknowledged that the posts did not, in fact, violate company policies.

AIID-711.title: NHTSA Opens New Probe into Tesla’s Autopilot Following More than a Dozen Fatal Accidents
AIID-711.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched a new investigation into Tesla's Autopilot following concerns that a previous recall of 2 million vehicles failed to adequately address safety risks. Regulators identified a 'critical safety gap' where the system's permissive capabilities were not matched by effective driver engagement monitoring, contributing to hundreds of crashes and at least 14 fatalities. The probe is examining whether Tesla's software updates were sufficient to prevent foreseeable driver misuse and whether the marketing of the system creates unrealistic expectations of autonomy.
AIID-711.description: The NHTSA has linked Tesla's Autopilot to over a dozen fatalities and hundreds of crashes, prompting a new investigation into the adequacy of Tesla's December recall of 2 million vehicles. The probe reports that Tesla’s driver-assist system led to avoidable crashes involving visible hazards, suggesting a critical safety gap between driver expectations and the system’s capabilities. The investigation will assess if Tesla’s recall remedies were sufficient to address these safety risks.

AIID-711.aiGoalJustification: The primary goal of Tesla's Autopilot is to automate driving tasks such as steering, accelerating, and braking within a lane, which falls under Autonomous Driving, while also assisting the driver in navigating highways.

AIID-712.summary: Meta's AI chatbot in Facebook Messenger was found to be hallucinating false sexual harassment allegations against various New York state lawmakers. The chatbot fabricated specific details, including non-existent investigations and professional consequences, when prompted with the names of officials. While Meta acknowledged the technology is new and prone to errors, the incident has prompted calls for greater accountability regarding AI-generated misinformation.
AIID-712.description: Meta's AI chatbot in Facebook Messenger falsely accused multiple state lawmakers of sexual harassment, fabricating incidents, investigations, and consequences that never occurred. These fabricated stories, discovered by City & State, sparked outrage among the affected lawmakers and raised concerns about the reliability of the chatbot. Meta acknowledged the errors and committed to ongoing improvements.

AIID-712.natSecSummary: Meta's AI chatbot fabricated detailed, false sexual harassment allegations against several New York state lawmakers. While causing personal distress and highlighting generative AI misinformation risks, the incident was an unintentional technical hallucination with negligible direct impact on national security.
AIID-712.natSecImminenceJustification: The immediate incident has been identified and addressed by Meta, representing an ongoing strategic concern regarding AI-generated misinformation rather than an active crisis.

AIID-712.natSecSocietalJustification: The chatbot generated defamatory content about individuals, which could minorly erode trust in public information, but did not cause large-scale civil unrest or systemic human rights violations.

Management.Explanation: Deploying generative AI features before resolving known hallucination issues.
Shifting the safety and verification burden to users via general warnings.

Technology.Explanation: The underlying LLM inherently fabricates details without verification.
Inconsistent safety behavior across mobile, desktop, and login states.

Data Inputs.Explanation: The model generated text without grounding in verifiable online sources.
Prompts with names and sensitive terms easily triggered false narratives.

Human Factors.Explanation: Users combined politician names with sensitive words, triggering safety gaps.

Process and Methods.Explanation: Lack of robust guardrails to block generation of defamatory content.
Testing failed to catch variations in desktop versus mobile app responses.

Regulatory Environment.Explanation: Current laws do not specifically address AI-generated defamatory content.
